source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Constitution at Work, Ch. 10 (The Philosophy of the Constitution).

sections.heading: 1. The Political Philosophy
points: The Constitution is not just a legal document but embodies a **political philosophy** — a vision of a just society.
It reflects the values of the **freedom struggle**: liberty, equality, fraternity, social justice, secularism and democracy.
It is best understood by reading the **Preamble** and the goals it sets.

sections.heading: 2. The Preamble — Core Values
points: The **Preamble** declares India a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic** (socialist & secular added by 42nd Amendment, 1976).

sub: **Liberty** — of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.
**Fraternity** — assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation.

points: The Preamble is the 'soul' / key to the Constitution.

sections.heading: 3. Key Features of the Philosophy
points: **Individual freedom** — protected through Fundamental Rights.
**Social justice** — protection of the weaker sections (reservations, abolition of untouchability).
**Secularism** — an Indian model: state has no religion, treats all religions equally, can intervene for reform.
**Universal franchise and democracy** — remarkable in a poor, diverse, largely illiterate society at Independence.
**National identity** — unity in diversity.

sections.heading: 4. Criticisms and Strengths
points: Criticisms: the Constitution is **unwieldy, un-Indian/borrowed, elitist** in parts.
But it is **not a slavish imitation** — it adapted borrowed features to Indian conditions and made bold commitments (universal franchise, social justice).
It is a **means to achieve social transformation** — a 'social revolution' document.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Preamble: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
Values: Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity.
Socialist & Secular added by 42nd Amendment (1976).
Indian secularism = state has no religion + equal treatment + can reform.
Constitution = instrument of social transformation (social justice + individual freedom).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The words **Socialist and Secular** were added to the Preamble by the **42nd Amendment (1976)**.
The Preamble's values = **Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity**.
**Indian secularism** allows the state to **intervene** in religion for reform (not strict separation).
The Constitution is not merely borrowed — it **adapted** features to Indian needs.
